legal-guardrail enforcement across request and output paths
gates.verdict_basis: No P0. Two P1 found AT 6103ad8 and reproduced. Both are fixed in 218d3f9, not here. Two P2 remain open by decision rather than oversight: A1 accepted as a pre-launch product posture, C1 valid but unreachable and deferred with a named remediation. The earlier label CONDITIONAL_PASS was replaced because it read as a property of this SHA when it was a summary of what the review turned up.

findings.claim: Three prohibited concepts reach the answer path instead of being refused.

reproduction.method: ran detectPersonalizedAdviceRequest against the three named phrasings plus refuse/allow controls, before any change
triggers: Give me a guaranteed 10% annual return strategy for Apple
What will Apple trade at next year?
Tell my brother to dump Apple and move everything into bonds
reproduction.observed_after: all three return true (refused); the must-allow controls still return false

findings.cause: Each prohibited concept had one phrasing covered and its neighbour uncovered: 'guaranteed' and 'return' had to be adjacent, definitive-price detection required a numeral or the word 'where', and third-party framing existed only in Korean (IR-034).
findings.fix: Three patterns added covering guaranteed-return with intervening text, future-tense price questions without a numeral, and English third-party instruction framing.

findings.claim: Float comparison of stored and incoming values can treat a genuine revision as unchanged.

reproduction.method: control assertion in the regression test rather than a live ingest, because no series reaches the magnitude required
reproduction.observed_before: Number("10000000000000.000001") === Number("10000000000000.000002") is true, so the two readings compare equal
reproduction.observed_after: sameDecimalValue distinguishes them while still treating 1.50 and 1.5 as equal

findings.cause: The column stores six decimals; a double carries 15-17 significant digits, so precision is lost above ~10^10.
findings.fix: sameDecimalValue() compares normalised decimal strings; both Number() comparison sites replaced.
findings.reachability: LATENT — no current series is near that magnitude. Fixed because the failure is silent: no error, no revision row, and a ledger that looks consistent while missing a figure.
regression_tests: tests/decimalValueIdentity.test.ts (4 pass, including the control that proves the old comparison collapses)

findings.claim: A database password shorter than the eight-character redaction floor survives into persisted ingestion errors.

reproduction.method: redacted a connection URI carrying a seven-character password
reproduction.observed_after: password replaced; scheme, user, host, port and database name preserved

findings.cause: Redaction was by exact value only, and the length floor that prevents '[REDACTED]' soup also exempted short real passwords.
findings.fix: CONNECTION_URI_PASSWORD redacts the userinfo password by shape. The length floor is unchanged and still governs value-based redaction.
regression_tests: tests/redactSecrets.test.ts (23 pass; 4 URI shapes, a preservation case and three non-secret controls)

findings.claim: signUp discloses whether an email is already registered, giving an enumeration oracle.

reproduction.method: read the code path; the thrown message is unconditional on an existing account
reproduction.observed: "An account with this email already exists" is returned to an unauthenticated caller

findings.why_not_fixed: The standard remedies require email verification, which is a Human Gate (bulk messaging), and the alternative generic failure strands a user who has forgotten they registered. This is a product decision, not a code fix. signIn is unaffected — it already refuses to reveal which field failed or that a lockout occurred.
findings.revisit: Required before public launch; recorded with HG-009 in docs/HUMAN_GATE_QUEUE.md.

findings.claim: assertValidClaim performs no content-level validation, so a prohibited claim could be stored.
findings.downgrade_reason: Structurally accurate — validation covers shape only (FACT needs sourceId, CALCULATION needs evidence, INFERENCE needs confidence in range) — but unreachable: nothing constructs such a claim, the request guardrail refuses those questions at input, and no page renders claims.
findings.why_not_fixed_now: The obvious fix, reusing ADVICE_OUTPUT_PATTERNS from src/server/verify/evaluate.ts, would import the v2 shadow layer into v1 domain, which the architecture boundary test forbids. Copying the list into the ledger would create a second copy of a guardrail vocabulary that must never diverge — duplicated pattern lists are what the GUARDRAIL_COVERAGE cluster is made of.
findings.remediation: Extract one shared prohibited-language policy module consumed by three callers: the request guardrail, the output scanner and the ledger. A deliberate refactor, not a change to make under a frozen candidate.

clean_areas: sessions use 32 random bytes, rotate on login, and set HttpOnly/SameSite=Lax/Secure-in-production cookies
/admin requires a validated session and ADMIN_EMAILS membership, failing closed when unset
passwords use salted scrypt with constant-time comparison
refusals survive the domain-to-page boundary; the page cannot substitute its own answer
FACT and CALCULATION verification re-fetch and recompute rather than trusting stored text
original observations are protected by a partial unique index; uniqueness races are idempotent
only .env.example is committed; the destructive-test guard refuses missing, identical, non-disposable and production-like targets

findings.claim: The new third-party patterns keyed on a possessive pronoun from a fixed list, so close paraphrases still reached the answer path.

triggers: Advise your brother to liquidate his Tesla position.
Can you promise my brother a 10% annual return?
reproduction.observed_after: all four refused; every must-allow control still answers

findings.cause: A proper name, an unlisted pronoun and a kinship term with no pronoun all bypass a possessive-pronoun requirement. Who the third party is was never the point. Separately, 'promise' carries the guarantee meaning and only 'guarantee' was covered.
findings.fix: The instruction pattern no longer requires a possessive and is bounded to a single sentence; a kinship-term pattern was added; 'promise' is covered when it is promised to a person, which is what separates it from 'the new fab promises better returns'.
regression_tests: tests/askMarketConceptCoverage.test.ts - 7 new must-refuse cases; removing the new patterns fails 11 assertions

findings.claim: The new patterns refuse legitimate research questions.

reproduced.input: What will happen if US markets close tomorrow?
reproduced.cause: a bare 'close' in the price pattern; a closing PRICE needs the preposition - close at, close above - to mean anything

reproduced.input: Advise my analyst to hold GDP constant when comparing the two scenarios.
reproduced.detail: The new hold pattern correctly ignores the analytical sense - the identical sentence with 'the team' in place of 'my analyst' answers normally. The refusal comes from the advisor-proxy pattern, which long predates this round and exists to block 'what would my broker recommend'. Left unchanged: outside the reviewed range, placed deliberately, and loosening an advice guardrail for one methodology question is not a trade to make under a frozen candidate. Pinned by test so it stays a decision rather than an accident.

rejected.input: What guaranteed benefits affect the pension fund's expected return?
rejected.detail: The gap between 'guaranteed' and 'return' is 41 characters, past the pattern's 40-character bound. Checked before being acted on; did not reproduce.

regression_tests: tests/askMarketConceptCoverage.test.ts - 7 must-answer cases plus a pin for the pre-existing advisor-proxy behaviour

findings.claim: sameDecimalValue does not parse the decimal syntax the adapters actually deliver, so a superseded value can bypass the rollback guard.

reproduction.method: checked reachability in the adapters before accepting the claim - both normalizers validate with Number.isFinite(Number(raw)) and then persist the ORIGINAL string, so 1e5, +1 and .5 all arrive verbatim
reproduction.observed_before: sameDecimalValue('100000','1e5') was false; a provider replaying 1e5 over a chain that had moved on to 110000 would have been written back in as a revision
reproduction.observed_after: true; and 1.234568 vs 1.2345678 now compare equal, because Decimal(20,6) is what the column keeps

findings.cause: The Gate A fix compared normalised decimal STRINGS. That removed the double-precision defect and assumed a spelling the data does not keep to.
findings.fix: Exact bigint arithmetic scaled to the column's six decimal places, rounding half away from zero as the column does. Unparseable input is treated as different unless the strings are identical, because a spurious revision is a visible row and a missed one is silence.
regression_tests: tests/decimalValueIdentity.test.ts - 8 syntax cases, precision cases and unparseable-input cases; reverting to Number() fails 4 tests, reverting to the Gate A string version fails 8

findings.claim: A connection URI with an empty username keeps its password.
findings.cause: The username character class required at least one character. The password was six characters, below the value-redaction floor, so no later phase caught it either.

findings.claim: The URI substitution corrupts prose containing a scheme://word:word@ grammar example.

reproduction.input: Parser syntax is proto://left:right@ followed by a host token.
reproduction.observed_before: proto://left:[REDACTED]@ followed by a host token.

findings.cause: Nothing was required after the '@', and this substitution runs before the other two phases, so no later step could restore the text.
findings.fix: A lookahead requires a host character after the '@'. Real connection URIs always have a host, so this costs nothing.
regression_tests: tests/redactSecrets.test.ts - reverting the regex fails 3 tests

gates.test_discrimination: The review asked whether any new test could still pass with its fix reverted. Checked by doing it: reverting the connection regex fails 3, reverting sameDecimalValue to Number() fails 4, reverting it to the Gate A string version fails 8, and removing the new guardrail patterns fails 11. The reviewer also observed that several must-ALLOW assertions pass under a reversion - that is what a negative control is, and they are kept as controls rather than counted as proof.
clean_areas: no catastrophic-backtracking construction among the new regexes - spans are bounded and character classes hold no nested ambiguous repetition
sameDecimalValue throws on none of the probed inputs
whitespace, trailing zeros, leading zeros, ordinary negatives and negative zero all handled
the connection regex handles ordinary usernames, one-character passwords, mixed-case schemes and schemes containing + . -
gates.sha_status_detail: This gate's verdict describes what the review FOUND at this SHA. It is not a statement that this SHA is clean. The fixes it produced are not contained in it, so this SHA is superseded and must never be attested.

chain: Gate A reviewed 6103ad8 and produced fixes -> candidate moved to 218d3f9
Gate B reviewed 218d3f9 and produced fixes -> candidate moves again
Gate C reviews the post-Gate-B candidate; its result is recorded in docs/REVIEW_ATTESTATION.json and .md
closure_conditions.why_gate_c_is_not_in_this_file: docs/REVIEW_ATTESTATION.json and .md are the only review paths on the RC preflight's evidence-only allowlist. This file is not, so a commit touching it after the candidate would invalidate the review coverage the preflight checks. Gate C therefore lands in the attestation, which is the mechanism designed for exactly that.
closure_requires: a gate that finds no P0 and no P1 requiring a code change at the candidate SHA
no executable commit after the reviewed candidate
remote CI green on exactly that SHA
an attestation whose reviewed code SHA is an ancestor of the attestation SHA, with every intervening path on the evidence-only allowlist

reading_rule: A gate entry records what a review found at one SHA. No gate entry ever makes its own SHA clean: a review that produced fixes is evidence AGAINST the SHA it examined. A clean candidate is one where a gate found nothing needing a code change, and only docs/REVIEW_ATTESTATION.json asserts that, checked against the commit graph by the RC preflight. UNKNOWN stays UNKNOWN.
